# Intentional exceptions to the fingerprint scan, one literal substring per line.
# Matched literally by `grep -F`, so they are exact strings, not regexes.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
#
# The scan in .github/workflows/ci.yml is deliberately narrow. Every entry here
# is a fingerprint that was found by review, judged safe on purpose, and written
# down so the decision is visible and reversible rather than silently encoded in
# a regex nobody reads.
#
# Adding a line here is a decision to publish that string. Do not add one to make
# a red build go green without asking why it was red.
#
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# sardar@aiden[t]ech.com
#
#   The repository owner's own address, and the author of all five commits.
#   It was found during the pre-publication scrub and offered for removal; the
#   owner chose to keep it, on the grounds that correct attribution of their own
#   work is worth more than the address not appearing. It is a personal work
#   mailbox, not a credential: it is not a token, it grants no access to this
#   repository or anything else, and rotating it does not remediate anything.
#
#   The cost is real and is recorded here rather than discovered later: if this
#   repository is ever made public, this address becomes world-readable and
#   harvestable for spam and phishing, and the commits will render as coming
#   from an unverified contributor because the address is not verified on the
#   GitHub account.
#
#   To reverse the decision: rewrite the author metadata to the GitHub noreply
#   address (Abaabeel@users.noreply.github.com, which GitHub verifies and which
#   preserves attribution), then delete this line. That is one more
#   `git filter-repo --email-callback` pass followed by a force-push, and it is
#   only cheap to perform while the repository is still private. See GIT-PLAN.md
#   section 8 for why a force-push is necessary but not sufficient on its own.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
sardar@aiden[t]ech.com
